text:
By the chances, this was Philadelphia's game by a mile. The Flyers had 68 shot attempts to 39, 5.99 expected goals (the quality of chances) to 2.02, and in our replays of every shot they win it 94% of the time. Edmonton won 5-2. Tristan Jarry is most of the explanation, and Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl are the rest.

The Oilers built the lead early with their power play. Draisaitl scored at 8:08 of the first from McDavid and Evan Bouchard, Vasily Podkolzin added a second power-play goal at 13:22, and Zach Hyman, with McDavid and Bouchard again, made it 3-0 before the period ended for his 500th career point. Dan Vladar faced 20 shots all night and let in four, two goals worse than expected.

Then the Flyers took over. Cole Knuble scored midway through the second and Noah Cates made it 3-2 at 17:12, with Matvei Michkov, the subject of a week of trade noise that the team says it isn't acting on, setting it up. Michkov played 23:48 and Philadelphia had 3.56 expected goals with him on the ice against 0.13. But Draisaitl scored 1:07 into the third, and the Flyers spent the rest of the period piling up chances: 2.90 expected goals to 0.30 in the third alone. Sean Couturier had a 62% look that missed the net. Philadelphia went 0 for 8 on the power play, which by itself was worth 2.41 expected goals. Travis Konecny, to Charlie O'Connor of PHLY Sports: "I mean, I don't know how many looks I had. Way too many to not put one in."

Jarry made 34 saves and finished 4.0 goals better than expected, the biggest contribution to the win by a distance, a night after Devon Levi's shutout in Toronto. McDavid's goal with 68 seconds left, a 2% chance, was the least likely of the night and stretched his point streak again.

That's five straight for Edmonton and two wins over the Flyers in five days. For Rick Tocchet's team, this is the frustrating kind of loss: better for most of the night, and nothing to show for it.
headline: Jarry stands tall as Oilers steal one in Philadelphia
